processing: Pan-fired and pressed flat in a hot wok in the Longjing method, by hand or by machine.
harvest_season: Spring, from March; pre-Qingming lots bring the best price, followed by those picked before Guyu.
appearance_wet: Tender, flat green buds and leaves that soften and open in the water.
taste_profile: Fresh and mellow with a chestnut note and a clean, gentle finish.

brewing.notes: A glass or open cup with water around 80 C. Pour gently and drink before the leaf stews.

vintage_note: Sold as the current year's spring tea, graded by picking date: before Qingming, then before Guyu. Only West Lake leaf may be called Xihu Longjing, so tea from this zone sells as Longjing at much lower prices. Best drunk within a year.
description:
Qiantang is one of the three legal production zones for Longjing, alongside West Lake and Yuezhou. It takes in the Hangzhou-area counties around the famous core, such as Xiaoshan, Yuhang, Fuyang and Lin'an, and is usually the place people mean when they speak of good Longjing without the West Lake price.

The method is the same as elsewhere: leaf pressed flat against a hot wok until it dries smooth and straight. What differs is the land, and the plant can differ too, since Longjing is made from several cultivars.

The usual description is a green, flat, smooth leaf with a chestnut scent and a mellow, brisk cup. Compared with the best West Lake tea it is generally simpler and less layered, but a careful spring lot is a real pleasure. Use cool water and do not rush it.

The trap runs the other way too: tea from here is sometimes sold as West Lake Longjing at inflated prices. Buy it honestly, as Qiantang or plain Longjing, with a clear picking date, and judge it by the cup.
history: The zone is a modern legal category rather than an old tea name. The national geographical indication standard for Longjing divides production into West Lake, Qiantang and Yuezhou, and it reserves the West Lake name for the first. Within that system Yuezhou produces the most, Qiantang comes second, and West Lake is only a few per cent of the total, according to one of the drafters of the standard. County lists vary between accounts, with some adding Tonglu, Jiande and Chun'an.
